name: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026
short_description: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026 is a verified women-only Half Marathon plus family-distance race in Singapore, confirmed for 1 November 2026 with open registration.
ai_summary: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026 is a women-focused road race at Singapore's National Stadium / The Kallang precinct, confirmed for 1 November 2026 with a 4:30am start. Organized by Great Eastern, it centers on a 21.1km women-only Half Marathon alongside 10km and 5km categories, plus family-oriented 2km "Mummy+Me" and 100m "Princess Dash" events. Registration is open directly via the official website.

core_facts.venue: Singapore National Stadium / The Kallang (4:30am start)

pros: Women-only Half Marathon category alongside family-friendly 2km and 100m events broadens participation beyond a typical marathon field
Registration is open directly via the official site, no third-party platform required
cons: Five distinct categories at one event may make choosing the right entry confusing for first-time participants
Only two sources cited for verification (official site plus one aggregator)

research_highlights: Route starts and finishes at Singapore Sports Hub/National Stadium; the 2025 edition's half marathon route passed the Barrage, Marina Bay and Gardens by the Bay, with an elevation section over Sheares Bridge just after the 14km mark noted as new and challenging for many runners.
Half marathon flag-off has typically been very early (around 5:15am), with runners arriving 45 minutes to an hour beforehand to enter the start pens.
Weather is consistently reported as warm and humid at race time, even in the early morning hours, based on multiple year's reviews (2024, 2025 editions).

The event is known for generous post-race and race-village perks: past editions have included free-flow oat milk, yoghurt, cheese, 100PLUS drinks, breakfast boxes, a 'powder room' for freshening up, and massage stations (though massage queues can be long).

Race has multiple categories including 21.1km (Elite/Open), 10km, 5km, a 2km Mummy & Me, and a 100m Princess Dash for young girls, and past editions sold out (fully subscribed) well ahead of race day.
research_watchouts: Massage stations at the race village have had very long queues in past editions, making them impractical for some runners.
Humid, sticky conditions at flag-off time have been repeatedly noted by participants, even in the early morning hours before sunrise.
New elevation additions to the half-marathon course (e.g., Sheares Bridge introduced in a past edition) can catch runners off guard if they haven't trained for elevation.
Some hydration-station gels have differed in brand from what runners are used to, so those with specific nutrition needs may want to carry their own.

faqs.question: Is the Great Eastern Women's Run open to men?
faqs.answer: The race's headline 21.1km Half Marathon category is women-only, consistent with the event's name and positioning. The event also includes 10km and 5km categories plus family-oriented 2km and 100m events, so check the official race website directly for each category's specific eligibility rules before registering.

faqs.question: What time does the Great Eastern Women's Run start?
faqs.answer: The race starts early, at 4:30am, from Singapore's National Stadium / The Kallang precinct, confirmed for 1 November 2026. Early starts are common for Singapore road races to avoid the heat and humidity of daytime running, so plan your travel and warm-up time accordingly.

faqs.question: What distances can I run at the Great Eastern Women's Run?
faqs.answer: Five categories are offered: a 21.1km women-only Half Marathon, a 10km, a 5km, a 2km "Mummy+Me" run, and a 100m "Princess Dash" for children. This spread makes the event suitable for competitive runners, casual participants, and families attending together at the same race morning.
